Index confirms lectures 6 (Turing machines), 7 (decidability), 8 (undecidability), and 9 (mapping reducibility and Rice theorem). Slides credited to Prof. Nancy Lynch; index rather than linked PDFs read.
Sections 1 and 2 describe historical calculi, universality, halting undecidability, complexity.
Sections 2.3 and 2.4.1–2.4.3: universality, diagonal and Turing original circle-free versus contemporary halting formulation; 2025 revision verified.
Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society s2-42, 230-265; original paper provenance and date; full reasoning on SEP.

claim_evidence.anchor: no algorithm can make that promise for every program and every input in a sufficiently general model of computation.
claim_evidence.source_locator: SEP Turing Machines §2.4.3 standard halting theorem; Computability and Complexity §2.4 diagonal halting set.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: SEP Turing Machines §2.4.3 standard halting theorem; Computability and Complexity §2.4 diagonal halting set.

claim_evidence.anchor: We can even decide the halting question for carefully restricted programming languages.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Universality is a hypothesis; restricted finite-state models analyzed in companion.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Universality is a hypothesis; restricted finite-state models analyzed in companion.

claim_evidence.anchor: A universal machine can read such a description, together with some input data, and simulate the described machine.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Turing On Computable Numbers §§6–7 universal machine; SEP Turing Machines §2.3.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Turing On Computable Numbers §§6–7 universal machine; SEP Turing Machines §2.3.

claim_evidence.anchor: It may halt by accepting or rejecting; either counts as halting.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Exact modern HALT definition in companion; applies to designated halting states.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Exact modern HALT definition in companion; applies to designated halting states.

claim_evidence.anchor: H always terminates.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Hypothetical totality is the premise of diagonal proof; SEP §2.4.3.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Hypothetical totality is the premise of diagonal proof; SEP §2.4.3.

claim_evidence.anchor: If H says Q will halt, D deliberately loops forever.
claim_evidence.source_locator: D construction with branch inversion; SEP §2.4.3.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. D construction with branch inversion; SEP §2.4.3.

claim_evidence.anchor: Now give D its own description.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Diagonal self-application in companion; universality and machine coding from Turing and SEP §2.4.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Diagonal self-application in companion; universality and machine coding from Turing and SEP §2.4.

claim_evidence.anchor: if D halts, it must not halt.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Diagonal contradiction: H(d,d)=0 iff D(d) halts.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Diagonal contradiction: H(d,d)=0 iff D(d) halts.

claim_evidence.anchor: if D does not halt, it must halt.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Diagonal contradiction other case H(d,d)=1 iff D(d) diverges.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Diagonal contradiction other case H(d,d)=1 iff D(d) diverges.

claim_evidence.anchor: We derived a contradiction from the existence of a *total* decision procedure
claim_evidence.source_locator: Theorem in companion; totality and correctness both essential.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Theorem in companion; totality and correctness both essential.

claim_evidence.anchor: The same construction then gives an input on which the detector's claimed total correctness cannot hold.
claim_evidence.source_locator: SEP Computability and Complexity §2.4, diagonal construction defeats arbitrary solver.
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: SEP Computability and Complexity §2.4, diagonal construction defeats arbitrary solver.

claim_evidence.evidence_detail: SEP Computability and Complexity §2.4, diagonal halting set K and reference to Cantor.

claim_evidence.anchor: there are countably many programs but far more sets of strings.
claim_evidence.source_locator: Finite program encodings are countable; powerset of countably infinite set uncountable (Cantor).
claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Independent proof provided in the lecture companion. Finite program encodings are countable; powerset of countably infinite set uncountable (Cantor).

claim_evidence.anchor: The bounded question is decidable because you have placed a finite upper limit on the observation.

claim_evidence.evidence_detail: Finite simulation is not an algorithm for unbounded HALT; exact distinction in companion.
